title: Key Lime Filling
cScaleSummary: C2 because the 3 large eggs contribute cholesterol. At approximately 186 mg cholesterol per egg, the recipe contains about 558 mg cholesterol total, or about 70 mg per serving across 8 servings.
ldlActiveSummary: Not LDL-Active because this is a dessert filling built around eggs, sugar, citrus juice, and fat-free sweetened condensed milk. It is reduced in saturated fat compared with a traditional filling, but it is not fiber-forward and does not include meaningful LDL-supportive ingredients.
intro: A bright, creamy key lime-style filling made from regular grocery-store limes. Extra lime zest and a touch of lemon juice recreate the aromatic tartness associated with traditional Key limes while keeping the recipe lower in saturated fat and cholesterol.

stepGroups.title: Instructions
items: Add the fresh lime juice ({{quantity:fresh-lime-juice}}), fresh lemon juice ({{quantity:fresh-lemon-juice}}), and finely grated lime zest ({{quantity:finely-grated-lime-zest}}) to a mixing bowl.
Whisk in the granulated sugar ({{quantity:granulated-sugar}}), cornstarch ({{quantity:cornstarch}}), and kosher salt ({{quantity:kosher-salt}}) until smooth.
Allow the mixture to rest for 10 minutes so the zest can release its aromatic oils.
Whisk in the large eggs ({{quantity:large-eggs}}) until fully combined.
Whisk in the fat-free sweetened condensed milk ({{quantity:fat-free-sweetened-condensed-milk}}) until the filling is smooth and uniform.
Pour the filling into a prepared baked crust.
Bake at 325°F for 14 to 18 minutes, until the center reaches 160°F and the filling is set around the edges with a slight jiggle in the center.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.
